Harvest chef Patrick Roney: How to make citrus cured carp

Beverages reporter Bailey Loosemore is visiting the kitchens of local chefs to gather their recipes and advice on cooking with beer and bourbon. Find a new Spirited Kitchen video online every other Wednesday, and let us know how your home experiments go using #SpiritedKitchen.

For this episode, we stopped by Harvest at 624 E. Main St. to learn how to make citrus cured carp with a wheat berry salsa using Sierra Nevada's Otra Vez beer.

► RELATED: Find more recipes from the Spirited Kitchen series

Have a recipe suggestion? Reach reporter Bailey Loosemore at 502-582-4646 or bloosemore@courier-journal.com.


Citrus cured Lake Barkley Silver Carp with tomato, jalapeno and wheat berry salsa

Recipe from Patrick Roney, executive chef at Harvest

Serves 4

 * 1 orange
 * 1 lemon
 * 1 lime
 * 4 tomatoes
 * 2-3 jalapenos
 * 1 cucumber
 * 1 bunch cilantro
 * 2 ounces extra virgin olive oil
 * 1 ounce coarse sea salt
 * 1 cup wheat berries
 * 6 ounces fresh carp
 * 1 can Sierra Nevada Otra Vez

Cook wheat berry in 1 gallon of boiling salted water for about one hour or until tender. (Tip: Soak them in cold water overnight.)

Slice carp very thin horizontally until you have eight slices. Line your slices up on a flat sheet tray lined with plastic wrap. Zest the skin of your citrus evenly over the fish, then squeeze half of the juices on them. Season with fresh ground pepper and coarse sea salt. Cover again with plastic and rest for an hour in the fridge.

Slice the jalapeno into thin rings. Dice two tomatoes without seeds. Dice the cucumber without seeds. Toss all of them together with some leaves of cilantro and the remaining citrus juices. Add olive oil and season, toss again. Add an equal amount of wheat berry to vegetables, let the flavors marry in the fridge for 10 min.

Throw two very ripe tomatoes into a blender. Add all of your cucumber and jalapeno scraps in as well. Pour 4 ounces of beer in and season with sea salt. Blend on high for one minute. Pour into a fine mesh strainer lined with cheese cloth. Let sit in refrigerator for one hour to drip.

Assemble your salsa into bowls. Fold your fish over itself so it looks like a ribbon and place on top. Garnish with fresh lime, jalapeno and cilantro. Upon serving tableside, pour your tomato-beer water over top.

Kingfish Sashimi w Nước Chấm Coconut Serving Suggestions

Kingfish Sashimi w Nước Chấm, Coconut & Curry Leaf


By Darren Purchese

A Darren Purchese original whipped up at Christmas 2025 along with a selection of other seafoods. It is light and delicious and works so well as a sharing dish, you could pair it with a bread or seed crackers, but it does actually stand up on its own.

Ensure you order sashimi grade kingfish from your fishmonger, and pop it in the freezer for 30 minutes to firm up before slicing so you can get it nice and thin. The dressing is a slight variation on the classic Nước Chấm Vietnamese dressing, and we added curry leaves because we loved the flavour and we had some in the garden.


Time


1


hour

Degree of Difficulty


Easy


Save


2

Print Recipe


Share Recipe


Ingredients


Servings


metric

imperial

Template is not defined.

metric imperial

KINGFISH SASHIMI

300g kingfish, sashimi grade

NướC CHấM

2tbsp caster sugar

3tbsp boiling water

2tbsp rice wine vinegar

2tbsp fish sauce

½ garlic clove, microplane grated

1 birdseye chilli, finely chopped w seeds in or out

2tbsp lime juice, fresh

1tbsp coriander stalks, finely chopped

CRISPY CURRY LEAVES

40 curry leaves, fresh

750g grapeseed oil

CURRY LEAF OIL

2 cup coriander leaves, washed and dried

200g grapeseed oil

25 crispy curry leaves, see above recipe

ASSEMBLY

100g coconut milk

1

For the fish preparation... place the fish into a container and freeze for 30 minutes. Remove from the freezer and transfer to a cutting board, user a sharp knife to cut thin slices of the raw fish. Place the slices onto a plate, cover and refrigerate until assembly time.


2

For the Vietnamese dipping sauce... place the sugar into a small bowl and pour over the boiling water. Stir the mix until the sugar has dissolved. Add the remaining ingredients and reserve.


3

For the crispy curry leaves... to prepare the curry leaves, heat the oil to 170°C. Add the curry leaf sprigs in batches and fry until bright green and crispy, about 10 seconds. Remove from the oil and place on paper towel to drain and cool.


4

For the curry leaf oil... blanch the coriander in boiling water for 10 seconds, then strain and submerge in the ice bath to cool. Drain well and squeeze out the excess water. Meanwhile, heat the grapeseed oil in a small saucepan to 60°C. Place the coriander leaves, warm oil and crispy curry leaves into a blender. Blend on high speed for 1-2 minutes until smooth and the oil is a deep green colour. Pour the oil through a lined sieve and set aside to strain. Season with a pinch of crushed salt flakes, to taste.


5

To assemble... arrange the sliced fish onto a serving plate. Spoon a few tablespoons of the Vietnamese dipping sauce and then spoon over the coconut milk. Add a few teaspoons of the curry oil over the top and dress the plate with fresh coriander and the reserved crispy curry leaves. Serve immediately.
